title: Places & Getting Around
description: Where you'll be going, from the market to the airport, and left, right and straight on to get there.

items.registerNotes: Pasar malam is a night market. A supermarket is just supermarket in speech.
items.cultureNote: At a traditional pasar prices are open to bargaining, unlike in shops and minimarkets.

items.english: small eatery, food stall; small shop
items.registerNotes: A warung makan sells meals, a warung kopi (warkop) coffee and snacks, and a warteg cheap home-style food you point to.
items.cultureNote: At many warungs you eat first and pay as you leave, saying what you had.

items.registerNotes: Short for bandar udara (air port), which is what the signs say.

items.pitfallNote: Only for trains. A bus station is a terminal, and a bus stop is a halte.

items.registerNotes: From Dutch, like kantor and handuk. Haltenya di mana? (Where's the bus stop?)
In names the kind of place comes first: Hotel Melati, Pasar Baru, Bank Mandiri. A cheaper guesthouse is a losmen or penginapan.
Literally sick house. For something minor, a klinik or the local puskesmas (community health centre) is quicker.
Spelled apotek, though older signs say apotik. The pharmacist can suggest something for a minor problem if you describe it.
A cash machine is an ATM, said a te em: Ada ATM dekat sini?
Part of many place names: kantor polisi (police station), kantor pos (post office), kantor imigrasi (immigration office).
Also a verb: Anaknya masih sekolah? (Is your child still at school?)
Pantai is the beach; the sea itself is laut. In names Pantai comes first: Pantai Kuta.

items.cultureNote: The call to prayer (azan) sounds from the masjid five times a day. Visitors take off their shoes and cover their arms and legs.
About one in ten Indonesians is Christian, and in parts of the east, such as Flores and North Sulawesi, most people are.

items.registerNotes: Kiri, Pak, or just Kiri, is how you ask a minibus or bus driver to pull over and let you off.
items.cultureNote: The left hand is for the toilet, so give, take and eat with your right.

items.registerNotes: Di sebelah kanan means on the right; belok kanan is turn right.
items.pitfallNote: Only the direction. Right as in correct is benar or betul.

items.registerNotes: Lurus saja or lurus terus means keep going straight.
Di depan hotel is in front of the hotel; behind is di belakang, next to is di sebelah. With time, depan means next: minggu depan.
